'''Katrin Wehrheim''' (born 1974) is an associate professor of mathematics at the [[University of California, Berkeley]]. Wehrheim's research centers around [[symplectic topology]] and [[gauge theory]], and they are known for work on [[pseudoholomorphic quilt]]s. With [[Dusa McDuff]], they have challenged the foundational rigor of a classic proof in [[symplectic geometry]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/20170209-the-fight-to-fix-symplectic-geometry/|magazine=Quanta|title=A Fight to Fix Geometry's Foundations: When two mathematicians raised pointed questions about a classic proof that no one really understood, they ignited a years-long debate about how much could be trusted in a new kind of geometry|first=Kevin|last=Hartnett|date=February 9, 2017}}.</ref> 

== Education and career ==
After attending school in [[Hamburg]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://archiv.abendblatt.de/ha/1988/xml/19881209xml/habxml881012_11189.xml|title=Hamburg ehrte seine jungen Sieger|date=9 December 1988|work=Hamburger Abendblatt|publisher=Springer|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090928153514/http://archiv.abendblatt.de/ha/1988/xml/19881209xml/habxml881012_11189.xml|archivedate=September 28, 2009|url-status=dead|accessdate=2009-11-19}}</ref> and studying at the [[University of Hamburg]] until 1995 and [[Imperial College]] until 1996, Wehrheim went to [[ETH Zürich]] for graduate studies. After almost dropping out to become an [[Rowing at the Summer Olympics|Olympic rower]], Wehrheim completed their PhD in 2002, under the joint supervision of [[Dusa McDuff]] and [[Dietmar Salamon]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=120235|title=Katrin Wehrheim - The Mathematics Genealogy Project|website=www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu|access-date=2018-12-05}}</ref>

Wehrheim was an instructor at [[Princeton University]] and member of the [[Institute for Advanced Study]]<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/katrin-wehrheim|title=Katrin Wehrheim|work=Scholars|date=9 December 2019 |publisher=Institute for Advanced Study|access-date=2024-04-01}}; note 2004 start date as a member</ref> before taking a tenure track position at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 2005.<ref name="WIM">{{Cite journal|last=Murray|first=Margaret A.M.|date=January 2009|title=A Celebration of Women in Mathematics at MIT|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200901/tx090100042p.pdf|journal=Notices of the AMS|publisher=American Mathematical Society|volume=56|issue=1|pages=42, 44, 45}}</ref> While they were at MIT, Wehrheim—who is openly gay—co-headed the 2008 Celebration of Women in Mathematics conference.<ref name="WIM"/><ref>{{Cite web|title=Katrin Wehrheim – Women In Math|url=https://math.mit.edu/wim/members/katrin-wehrheim/|access-date=2021-08-28|website=math.mit.edu}}</ref> Since 2013, Wehrheim has been teaching mathematics at the University of California, Berkeley.<ref name="berkeleyfaculty">{{Cite web|url=https://math.berkeley.edu/people/faculty/katrin-wehrheim|title=Katrin Wehrheim {{!}} Department of Mathematics at University of California Berkeley|website=math.berkeley.edu|access-date=2018-12-05}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
Wehrheim's PhD thesis in mathematics ''Anti-Self-Dual Instantons with Lagrangian Boundary Conditions'' won the 2002 ETH medal.<ref name=":0" /> In 2010, Wehrheim received the [[PECASE|Presidential Career Award PECASE]] from [[Barack Obama]] in a ceremony at the White House.<ref>{{cite press release|title=President Names Nation's Top Early Career Scientists and Engineers|date=November 9, 2010|publisher=National Science Foundation|url=https://www.nsf.gov/news/news_summ.jsp?cntn_id=117723|accessdate=2012-11-29}}</ref> In 2012, Wehrheim became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-09-01.</ref>
